citation.title: Slow-paced breathing reduces anxiety and enhances midfrontal alpha asymmetry, buffering responses to aversive visual stimuli

reported.what: breathing rate during the slow-paced (SB) and natural-breathing (RB) sessions, 6.00 and 14.76 breaths/min, n=17 healthy students; the plus-minus is not labelled SD or SEM anywhere in the paper, and the sentence names no period of the session

location.where: Results, first paragraph (manipulation check before the physiological results)
location.quote: The mean respiratory rate was 6.00 ± 0.11 breaths/min during SB condition and 14.76 ± 3.43 breaths/min during RB condition.

detail: The only breathing-rate numbers in the text are the two means above, printed with a plus-minus that no sentence labels as SD or SEM (the paper writes 'standard deviation (SD)' only for age and for its outlier rule), so the uncertainty cannot be assumed; the sentence also names no period of the 5 min breathing task or of the 2 min fixation periods, so the window cannot be placed either. The paper's other numbers are estimated marginal means of its own mixed models (RMSSD, CVRR, ETCO2, rLFA) or STAI-S and EEG measures the model does not carry, and the healthy group has no printed resting value with a labelled spread.
